meta.title: Madhva (Dvaita Vedanta) Guru Parampara
meta.subtitle: Compiled for the DGE project - scholarly, non-commercial
meta.conventions: Dates in CE. Confidence: high | medium | traditional. 'unknown' where sources do not supply a value. Contemporaries are auto-computed from lifespan/pontificate overlap.
meta.note: The tree backbone follows recited guru->disciple / pontifical succession. Shared early ancestors (counted separately by rival mathas) appear once, on the core trunk. Chitrapur Math is Advaita/Smarta and is intentionally excluded from this Dvaita lineage. The Dasa Parampara (Haridasa) branch has been built out as a sourced lineage (Sripadaraja/Vyasatirtha fountainheads -> Purandara & Kanaka -> the 18th-c. Dasakuta revival: Vijaya Dasa -> Gopala Dasa -> Jagannatha Dasa, with their principal disciples).
meta.primary_reference: B.N.K. Sharma, History of the Dvaita School of Vedanta and Its Literature; Narayana Panditacharya, Sumadhva Vijaya; official matha websites.

nodes.name: Narayana (Vishnu, as Hamsa)
nodes.contrib: Supreme source of all knowledge; the independent reality (Svatantra Tattva). Fountainhead of the Brahma Sampradaya.
sources: Sumadhva Vijaya
uttaradimath.org
nodes.role: Source of the sampradaya

nodes.name: Chaturmukha Brahma
nodes.contrib: Four-faced creator; highest created soul; first recipient of knowledge from Narayana.
sources: Sumadhva Vijaya
uttaradimath.org

nodes.name: Sanakadi (Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanatana, Sanatkumara)
nodes.contrib: The four mind-born Kumaras of Brahma; carried the jnana-parampara onward.
sources: Sumadhva Vijaya
uttaradimath.org

nodes.name: Durvasa
nodes.contrib: Puranic rishi; a link in the eternal knowledge-lineage.
sources: Sumadhva Vijaya
uttaradimath.org

nodes.name: Jnananidhi Tirtha
nodes.contrib: A teacher of the traditional mula-parampara, the lineage of gurus recited before Madhvacharya in the daily Guru-parampara stotra, holding the knowledge of Tattvavada across the ages.
sources: Sumadhva Vijaya
uttaradimath.org

nodes.name: Garuda-vahana Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Garuda-vahana Tirtha, a guru of the traditional mula-parampara recited before Madhvacharya, counted among the eternal teachers of the Vaishnava-Dvaita lineage.
sources: Sumadhva Vijaya
uttaradimath.org

nodes.name: Kaivalya Tirtha
nodes.contrib: A teacher of the traditional mula-parampara preceding Madhvacharya, named in the lineage of gurus through whom the knowledge of liberation (kaivalya) was carried.
sources: Sumadhva Vijaya
uttaradimath.org

nodes.name: Jnanesha Tirtha
nodes.contrib: A guru of the traditional mula-parampara recited before Madhvacharya, among the eternal preceptors of the lineage.
sources: Sumadhva Vijaya
uttaradimath.org

nodes.name: Para Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Para Tirtha, a teacher of the traditional mula-parampara preceding Madhvacharya in the recited lineage of gurus.
sources: Sumadhva Vijaya
uttaradimath.org
nodes.note: Rendered 'Pasa/Para Tirtha Yati' in some recitations.

nodes.name: Satyaprajna Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Satyaprajna Tirtha of the traditional mula-parampara, one of the last teachers named before the historical acharyas leading to Madhvacharya's own guru Achyutapreksha.
sources: Sumadhva Vijaya
uttaradimath.org
nodes.note: Do NOT confuse with the 20th-c. Uttaradi Matha pontiff of the same name (#39).

nodes.name: Prajna Tirtha (Prajnanidhi)
nodes.contrib: Immediate predecessor of Madhva's own guru in the recited parampara.
sources: Sumadhva Vijaya
uttaradimath.org

nodes.name: Achyutapreksha
nodes.contrib: Ekadandi ascetic head of a monastery at Udupi; the historical guru who ordained the young Vasudeva as Purnaprajna and directed him to compose a Brahmasutra commentary.
sources: Sumadhva Vijaya
uttaradimath.org

nodes.name: Madhvacharya
nodes.brindavana: No brindavana - tradition holds he withdrew to Badarikashrama (Badari)
nodes.place: Born at Pajaka, near Udupi; seat at Udupi Sri Krishna Matha
works: Dasa Prakaranas (incl. Tattva Sankhyana, Vishnu Tattva Vinirnaya, Mayavada Khandana)
nodes.contrib: Founder of Tattvavada / Dvaita Vedanta; doctrine of pancha-bheda (five real differences), Svatantra (Vishnu) vs Asvatantra, and taratamya (gradation of souls). Founded the Udupi Krishna Matha and the Ashta Matha system; seeded the Haridasa movement and a vast commentarial literature. 37 Sarvamula works.
sources: Wikipedia: Madhvacharya
B.N.K. Sharma, History of the Dvaita School of Vedanta

nodes.name: Trivikrama Panditacharya
nodes.contrib: Advaitin scholar won over after a days-long debate; became a lay disciple. His son Narayana Panditacharya wrote the Sumadhva Vijaya.
sources: Wikipedia

nodes.name: Narayana Panditacharya
nodes.contrib: Author of the principal traditional biography of Madhvacharya.
sources: Wikipedia

nodes.name: Padmanabha Tirtha
nodes.place: island in the Tungabhadra near Hampi / Anegundi
nodes.contrib: First systematic commentator on Madhva's terse texts; carried Dvaita into the Deccan.
sources: Wikipedia: Padmanabha Tirtha
uttaradimath.org

nodes.name: Narahari Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Regent/minister of the Eastern Ganga (Kalinga) kingdom; recovered the Rama-Sita icons for Madhva's mission; a progenitor of the Haridasa movement; traditionally an early figure in Yakshagana and Carnatic music.
sources: Wikipedia: Narahari Tirtha

nodes.name: Madhava Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Consolidated the institution after Madhva.
sources: uttaradimath.org
B.N.K. Sharma

nodes.name: Akshobhya Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Last direct disciple of Madhva to hold the peetha; famous debate victory over Vidyaranya of Sringeri on 'Tat tvam asi'; the bridge to Jayatirtha. Received diksha from Padmanabha Tirtha but succeeded Madhava Tirtha.
sources: Wikipedia: Akshobhya Tirtha

nodes.name: Jayatirtha (Tikacharya)
nodes.place: on the Kagina river, Kalaburagi district
works: Nyaya Sudha (magnum opus, ~24,000 granthas, on Anuvyakhyana)
Prameya Dipika / Nyaya Dipika (on Gita Bhashya)
nodes.contrib: Systematised and defended Dvaita to full dialectical parity. Nyaya Sudha became the central curricular text of every Madhva matha ('Sudha' study is the summit of the tradition).
sources: Wikipedia: Jayatirtha
B.N.K. Sharma

nodes.name: Vidyadhiraja Tirtha
nodes.contrib: FIRST BRANCH POINT. Had two chief disciples, Kavindra Tirtha and Rajendra Tirtha; from Rajendra descends the Vyasaraja Matha, from Kavindra the Uttaradi trunk (and later the Raghavendra line).
sources: uttaradimath.org
B.N.K. Sharma

nodes.name: Lakshmidhara Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Ordained by Padmanabha Tirtha to head the branch that becomes the Sripadaraja Matha (matha's own reckoning).
sources: https://madhwayati.blogspot.com/2019/06/a-14-sripadaraja-matha-mutt_14.html
https://madhwasakha.com/math-details/shri-sripadaraja-math/15

nodes.name: Sankarshana Tirtha
nodes.contrib: An early pontiff of the Sripadaraja Matha line, disciple of Lakshmidhara Tirtha and guru of Parashurama Tirtha; tradition places his vrindavana at Srinagar in Kashmir, reached on a northern tour.
sources: madhwasakha.com
madhwayati.blogspot.com
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/sripadaraja-mutt/sankarshana-tirtharu/

nodes.name: Parashurama Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Disciple of Sankarshana Tirtha and guru of Adiraja Tirtha; his vrindavana is at the Chandrapushkarini gadde, Srirangam.
sources: madhwasakha.com
madhwayati.blogspot.com
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/sripadaraja-mutt/sri-parashurama-tirtharu/

sources: madhwasakha.com
madhwayati.blogspot.com

nodes.contrib: Disciple of Satyavrata Tirtha and the guru who initiated the great Sripadaraja (Lakshminarayana Tirtha); his vrindavana is at Srirangam.

nodes.name: Sripadaraja (Lakshminarayana Tirtha)
nodes.contrib: Pioneer of the Haridasa movement and dasa-sahitya; credited with inventing the 'suladi' form; teacher of Vyasaraja; advisor to Saluva Narasimha.
sources: Wikipedia: Sripadaraja

nodes.name: Hayagreeva Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Pontifical successor of Sripadaraja at the Mulbagal seat.
sources: https://madhwayati.blogspot.com/2019/06/a-14-sripadaraja-matha-mutt_14.html
https://madhwasakha.com/math-details/shri-sripadaraja-math/15

nodes.contrib: Disciple of Sridhara Tirtha and guru of Gopalaswami Tirtha; his vrindavana is at Marandanahalli near Mulbagal.

https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/sripadaraja-mutt/sri-sripathi-theertharu/

nodes.name: Sridhara Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Disciple of Sripati Tirtha and guru of Sripati (the later) in the Sripadaraja Matha succession.

nodes.contrib: Disciple of Lakshmi Manohara Tirtha and guru of Lakshminatha Tirtha.

nodes.name: Lakshminatha Tirtha

nodes.contrib: Disciple of Gunanidhi Tirtha and guru of Prajnanidhi Tirtha; his vrindavana is at Mulbagal.

nodes.contrib: Disciple of Gunasaranidhi Tirtha and guru of Subodhanidhi Tirtha; his vrindavana is at the Narasimha Tirtha, Mulbagal, the matha's principal seat.
sources: madhwasakha.com

nodes.contrib: Disciple of Subodhanidhi Tirtha and guru of Sujnananidhi Tirtha; his vrindavana is at Mulbagal.
sources: madhwasakha.com

nodes.name: Sujnananidhi Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Disciple of Vairagyanidhi Tirtha and guru of Sugunanidhi Tirtha; his vrindavana is at Mulbagal.

nodes.name: Sudhinidhi Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Born Hariyappacharya, he took sannyasa in 1888 and entered his vrindavana at Erode in 1908; guru of Medhanidhi Tirtha.
sources: madhwasakha.com
madhwayati.blogspot.com

nodes.name: Medhanidhi Tirtha

https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/sripadaraja-mutt/medhanidhi-tirtharu/

nodes.name: Dayanidhi Tirtha
nodes.contrib: A law graduate who served as a sub-registrar before renouncing, he led the Sripadaraja Matha for 46 years (1926-1962) and was noted for his learning. Disciple of Medhanidhi Tirtha and guru of Satyanidhi Tirtha; his vrindavana is at Mulbagal.
sources: madhwasakha.com
madhwayati.blogspot.com
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/sripadaraja-mutt/dayanidhi-tirtharu/

nodes.name: Satyanidhi Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Disciple of Dayanidhi Tirtha and guru of Vijayanidhi Tirtha; his vrindavana is at Mulbagal.
sources: madhwasakha.com
madhwayati.blogspot.com

nodes.name: Vijayanidhi Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Disciple of Satyanidhi Tirtha (sannyasa 1980) and guru of Vignananidhi Tirtha.
sources: madhwasakha.com
madhwayati.blogspot.com
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/sripadaraja-mutt/vijayanidhi-theertharu/

nodes.name: Vignananidhi Tirtha
nodes.contrib: The 35th pontiff of the Sripadaraja Matha, born Bheemachar. Disciple of Vijayanidhi Tirtha and guru of Keshavanidhi Tirtha, he installed a Sripadaraja mrittika vrindavana at Rajarajeshwari Nagar, Bengaluru.
sources: madhwasakha.com
madhwayati.blogspot.com
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/sripadaraja-mutt/vijnananidhi-tirtharu/

nodes.name: Keshavanidhi Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Disciple of Vignananidhi Tirtha in the Sripadaraja Matha succession.
sources: madhwasakha.com
madhwayati.blogspot.com

nodes.name: Sujayanidhi Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Present incumbent (#38) of Sripadaraja Matha, w.e.f. 22 May 2021.
sources: https://madhwayati.blogspot.com/2021/05/sujayanidhi-teertharu-matha-sripadaraja.html
nodes.role: present incumbent (Sripadaraja Matha)

nodes.name: Kavindra Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Received the samsthana from Vidyadhiraja (Uttaradi's claim to the original throne).
sources: https://uttaradimath.org/parampara/sri-kavindra-tirtha
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kavindra_Tirtha

nodes.name: Vageesha Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Toured India propagating Dvaita; succeeded Kavindra Tirtha.
sources: https://uttaradimath.org/parampara/sri-vagisha-tirtha

nodes.name: Ramachandra Tirtha
nodes.contrib: SECOND BRANCH POINT. His disciple Vibudhendra founded the Kumbhakonam (Dakshinadi) matha - later the Raghavendra Matha.
sources: https://uttaradimath.org/parampara/sri-ramachandra-tirtha

nodes.name: Vidyanidhi Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Acquired lands near Raichur for the matha; honoured by the king of Anegundi.
sources: https://uttaradimath.org/parampara/sri-vidyanidhi-tirtha

nodes.name: Raghunatha Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Conferred the title 'Sripadaraja' on Lakshminarayana Tirtha.
sources: https://uttaradimath.org/parampara/sri-raghunatha-tirtha

nodes.name: Raghuvarya Tirtha
nodes.contrib: An early pontiff of the seat later known as the Uttaradi Matha, remembered for the tradition that the Bhimarathi river parted to let him cross while he carried the Moola Rama pooja-box on his shoulders — likened to the Yamuna giving way to Vasudeva bearing the infant Krishna. His vrindavana is in the Nava Brindavana at Anegundi.
sources: https://uttaradimath.org/parampara/sri-raghuvarya-tirtha
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/uttaradi-mutt/raghuvarya-tirtharu/

nodes.name: Raghuttama Tirtha (Bhavabodhacharya)
nodes.place: near Tirukoilur, Tiruvannamalai district, Tamil Nadu
nodes.contrib: Pre-eminent 'meaning-revealing' commentator; the Bhavabodha series.
sources: uttaradimath.org

nodes.name: Vedavyasa Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Extensive tours; ordained Krishnadvaipayanacharya; won villages for the matha.
sources: https://uttaradimath.org/parampara/sri-vedavyasa-tirtha

nodes.name: Vidyadhisha Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Prolific author (~11 works); spread Dvaita across South and North India.
sources: https://uttaradimath.org/parampara/sri-vidyadhisha-tirtha

nodes.name: Vedanidhi Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Ruled ~5 yrs 10 months; contemporary of Raghavendra Tirtha (met at Kumbhakonam).
sources: https://uttaradimath.org/parampara/sri-vedanidhi-tirtha

nodes.name: Satyavrata Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Instituted the 'Satya' prefix carried by all subsequent Uttaradi Math pontiffs.
sources: https://uttaradimath.org/parampara/sri-satyavrata-tirtha

nodes.name: Satyanidhi Tirtha
nodes.place: Kurnool district, Andhra Pradesh (orig. Nivrutti Sangama)
nodes.contrib: A contemporary of Raghavendra Tirtha, whom he once met at Kumbakonam. His vrindavana stood near the Nivriti Sangama, the confluence of the Krishna and Tungabhadra; when the original site was submerged by the Srisailam hydro-electric project it was rebuilt to the same design within the Uttaradi Matha premises at Kurnool.
sources: https://uttaradimath.org/parampara/sri-satyanidhi-tirtha
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/uttaradi-mutt/satyanidhi-tirtharu/

nodes.name: Satyanatha Tirtha
nodes.place: Veeracholapuram, Villupuram district, Tamil Nadu (bank of South Pennar)
nodes.contrib: A major dialectician of the line, author of the Abhinava Chandrika and other polemical works celebrated in his dhyana-shloka. Initiated by Satyanidhi Tirtha, he held the seat 1660-1673 and entered his vrindavana at Veeracholapuram in Tamil Nadu on Gita Jayanti; the site also enshrines images of Ramachandra and Mukhyaprana.
sources: https://uttaradimath.org/parampara/sri-satyanatha-tirtha
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/uttaradi-mutt/satyanatha-tirtharu/

nodes.name: Satyabhinava Tirtha
nodes.place: Nachiarkoil, near Kumbhakonam, Thanjavur district, Tamil Nadu
nodes.contrib: Codified 17 categories of daily temple worship with 64 sevaks.
sources: https://uttaradimath.org/parampara/sri-satyabhinava-tirtha

nodes.name: Satyapurna Tirtha
nodes.place: Kolhapur (Kolpur) village, Mahabubnagar district, Telangana (bank of Krishna)
nodes.contrib: Donated gold/diamond ornaments to temples across India.
sources: https://uttaradimath.org/parampara/sri-satyapoorna-tirtha

nodes.name: Satyavijaya Tirtha
nodes.place: Satyavijayanagaram (Arani), Tiruvannamalai district, Tamil Nadu (bank of Kaveri)
nodes.contrib: Of the Pandurangi family, initiated by Satyapurna Tirtha. When his senior Satyapriya Tirtha could not be located during Satyapurna's final days, Satyavijaya was brought forward; he in turn later gave the seat to Satyapriya on his return from a long northern tour. His vrindavana is at Satyavijayanagara (Arani) in Tamil Nadu.
sources: https://uttaradimath.org/parampara/sri-satyavijaya-tirtha
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/uttaradi-mutt/satyavijaya-tirtharu/

nodes.name: Satyapriya Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Prolific commentator; converted poet Ghanashyam from Advaita to Dvaita.
sources: https://uttaradimath.org/parampara/sri-satyapriya-tirtha

nodes.name: Satyabodha Tirtha
nodes.place: Savanur, Haveri district, Karnataka (matha named 'Satyabodha Matha')
nodes.contrib: Philosopher-yogi honoured by Hindu and Muslim rulers; mediated peace at the siege of Trichinopoly. The Savanur monastery is named Satyabodha Matha.
sources: https://uttaradimath.org/parampara/sri-satyabodha-tirtha

nodes.name: Satyasandha Tirtha
nodes.place: Mahishi, Tirthahalli taluk, Shivamogga district, Karnataka
nodes.contrib: Stressed unity among Madhva mathas; discouraged sectarian division.
sources: https://uttaradimath.org/parampara/sri-satyasandha-tirtha

nodes.name: Satyavara Tirtha
nodes.contrib: A short-tenured pontiff of the Uttaradi Matha (1794-1797), disciple of Satyasandha Tirtha and guru of Satyadharma Tirtha; his vrindavana is at Santhebidanur.
sources: https://uttaradimath.org/parampara/sri-satyavara-theertha

nodes.name: Satyadharma Tirtha
nodes.contrib: A pontiff of the Navaratna family (1797-1830) who wrote a commentary on the Bhagavata. His vrindavana at Holehonnur is built so that the amshas of Jayatirtha, Vadiraja, Raghavendra and Satyabodha are held to be present there, with a Shiva-Bhagirathi sannidhana beside the garbhagudi.
sources: uttaradimath.org
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/uttaradi-mutt/satyadharma-thirtharu/

nodes.name: Satyasankalpa Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Initiated by Satyadharma Tirtha of Holehonnur, he held the seat 1830-1841 and was succeeded by Satyasanthushta Tirtha. His vrindavana is at the Uttaradi Matha, Mysore.
sources: https://uttaradimath.org/parampara/sri-satyasankalpa-tirtha
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/uttaradi-mutt/satya-sankalparu/

nodes.name: Satyasanthushta Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Former Mysore court pandita; ruled ~8 months; improved the matha's finances.
sources: https://uttaradimath.org/parampara/sri-satyasanthushta-theertha

nodes.name: Satyaparayana Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Prolific author; restored the matha's finances and recovered mortgaged property.
sources: https://uttaradimath.org/parampara/sri-satyaparayana-theertha

nodes.name: Satyakama Tirtha
nodes.place: Atkur, near Raichur, Karnataka (bank of Krishna)
nodes.contrib: Disciple of Satyaparayana Tirtha and guru of Satyeshti Tirtha, holding the seat 1863-1871. His vrindavana is at Atkur near Raichur, on the Krishna, alongside those of Satyeshti and Satyaprajna.
sources: https://uttaradimath.org/parampara/sri-satyakama-tirtha
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/uttaradi-mutt/satyakama-tirtharu/

nodes.name: Satyeshti Tirtha
nodes.place: Atkur, near Raichur, Karnataka (bank of Krishna)
nodes.contrib: A short-tenured pontiff (1871-1872), disciple of Satyakama Tirtha and guru of Satyaparakrama Tirtha. His vrindavana is at Atkur on the Krishna.
sources: https://uttaradimath.org/parampara/sri-sathyestha-tirtha
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/uttaradi-mutt/satyesta-thirtharu/

nodes.name: Satyaparakrama Tirtha
nodes.place: Chittapur, Kalaburagi district, Karnataka (bank of Krishna)
nodes.contrib: Disciple of Satyeshti Tirtha, author of the Prameyamala and a stotra on Satyavrata Tirtha. He held the seat 1872-1879; his vrindavana is at Chittapur in the Kalaburagi region on the bank of the Krishna.
sources: https://uttaradimath.org/parampara/sri-satyaparakrama-tirtha
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/uttaradi-mutt/satya-parakrama/

nodes.name: Satyaveera Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Reformer; set the matha's chaturmasya start on Ashadha Krishna Dashami.
sources: https://uttaradimath.org/parampara/sri-satyaveera-tirtha

nodes.name: Satyadheera Tirtha
nodes.place: Atkur, near Raichur, Karnataka (bank of Krishna)
nodes.contrib: Disciple of Satyaveera Tirtha and, in his purvashrama, the father of the great Satyadhyana Tirtha. He led the seat 1886-1906; his vrindavana is at Atkur on the Krishna.
sources: https://uttaradimath.org/parampara/sri-satyadheera-tirtha
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/uttaradi-mutt/satyadheera-tirtha/

nodes.name: Satyajnana Tirtha
nodes.place: Rajahmundry, East Godavari district, Andhra Pradesh (bank of Godavari)
nodes.contrib: Famed for public 'Shalaakha Pariksha' exposition of Nyaya Sudha.
sources: https://uttaradimath.org/parampara/sri-satyajnana-tirtha

nodes.name: Satyadhyana Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Great 20th-c. organiser; led the Kumbakonam debate (1929-30); founded a Chair of Dvaita Vedanta at Benares and the Madhva Siddhanta Abhivriddhikarini Sabha; engaged with B.G. Tilak.
sources: uttaradimath.org

nodes.name: Satyaprajna Tirtha
nodes.place: Atkur, near Raichur, Karnataka (bank of Krishna)
nodes.contrib: Served as Divan (administrator) of the matha before ordination.
sources: https://uttaradimath.org/parampara/sri-satyapragna-tirtha

nodes.name: Satyabhijna Tirtha
nodes.contrib: The 40th pontiff of the Uttaradi Matha (1945-1948), disciple of Satyaprajna Tirtha and guru of the long-serving Satyapramoda Tirtha. His vrindavana is at Ranebennur.
sources: https://uttaradimath.org/parampara/sri-satyabhijna-tirtha
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/uttaradi-mutt/satyabhijna-thirtharu/

nodes.name: Satyapramoda Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Leading modern defender of Dvaita; founded the Jayateertha Vidyapeetha, Bangalore (1989); relocated older brindavanas during dam-building.
sources: uttaradimath.org

nodes.name: Satyatma Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Founded the Vishwa Madhwa Maha Parishat (1998); education, disaster-relief and rural-development programmes; pan-India discourses.
sources: uttaradimath.org
nodes.role: present incumbent (Uttaradi Matha)

nodes.name: Vibudhendra Tirtha
nodes.contrib: An early pontiff of the line that would later be called the Rayara Mutt (then the Vibudhendra Tirtha Mutt after him), remembered as a formidable debater who toured northern India establishing the Dvaita position. He identified and initiated the young Anantappa, the future Jitamitra Tirtha, entrusting him with a Narasimha saligrama for daily worship.
sources: https://madhwasakha.com/guru/shri-vibudhendra-teertharu/513
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/rayara-mutt-2/jitamitraru-2/

nodes.name: Jitamitra Tirtha
nodes.brindavana: Tirunelveli (no vrindavana; disappeared at Jitamitra Gadde, Shivapura)
nodes.contrib: Initiated by Vibudhendra Tirtha, whom he had served as a boy worshipping a Narasimha saligrama. Tradition counts him among the very few Madhva ascetics for whom no vrindavana exists: he is said to have vanished in deep meditation into a tree near Shivapura on the Krishna-Bhima confluence, a spot still venerated as the Jitamitra Gadde. He is held to be an amsha of Rudra.
sources: https://madhwasakha.com/guru/shri-jitamitra-teertharu/514
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/rayara-mutt-2/jitamitraru-2/

nodes.name: Raghunandana Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Successor of Jitamitra Tirtha, remembered chiefly for recovering the mutt's Moola Rama idol through his guru's grace after it had been carried off. His vrindavana is at Hampi.
sources: https://madhwasakha.com/guru/shri-raghunandana-teertharu/515
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/rayara-mutt-2/raghunandana-tirtharu/

nodes.name: Surendra Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Held the pontifical seat for an unusually long tenure. He was close to Vyasaraja Tirtha, in whose presence he worshipped, and it was from Vyasaraja that he obtained his own brilliant successor, the young ascetic renamed Vijayindra Tirtha. Vijayanagara rulers granted him several villages. His vrindavana is at Madurai.
sources: https://madhwasakha.com/guru/shri-surendra-teertharu/516
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/rayara-mutt-2/surendra-tirtharu/

nodes.name: Vijayindra (Vijayeendra) Tirtha
nodes.contrib: A polymath and relentless polemicist trained under Vyasatirtha and Surendra Tirtha, credited by tradition with 104 works across Vedanta, Purva Mimamsa, Nyaya and poetics and with mastery of the sixty-four arts. Holding the seat at Kumbakonam under the Thanjavur Nayakas, he is renowned for his debates with the Advaita scholar Appayya Dikshita; inscriptions record village grants won through his victories.
sources: Wikipedia: Vijayendra Tirtha
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vijayindra_Tirtha
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/granthagalu/vijayeendra-theertharu/

nodes.name: Sudhindra Tirtha
nodes.contrib: A pioneer of Dvaita poetics and drama who wrote more than eighteen works spanning alankara, kavya and Vedanta. He toured widely in debate, was honoured as Rajaguru at Gwalior, and received honours from many kings. Above all he was the teacher who taught the young Venkatanatha for three years and later initiated him as Raghavendra Tirtha. His vrindavana is in the Nava Brindavana at Anegundi.
sources: https://madhwasakha.com/guru/shri-sudheendra-teertharu/518
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudhindra_Tirtha
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/rayara-mutt-2/sudheendra-theertharu/

nodes.name: Raghavendra Tirtha (Rayaru)
nodes.contrib: The best known figure of the whole line, honoured as Parimalacharya for his commentary Parimala on Jayatirtha's Nyaya Sudha. Born Venkatanatha at Bhuvanagiri and trained by Sudhindra Tirtha, he left an oeuvre spanning commentaries on Madhva, Jayatirtha and Vyasatirtha, nine Khandarthas on the Upanishads, and a treatise on Purva Mimamsa, besides devaranamas composed under the signature Venu Gopala. He entered his vrindavana alive at Manchale (Mantralaya) in 1671, where his shrine draws vast numbers of pilgrims to this day.
sources: Wikipedia: Raghavendra Tirtha
srsmatha.org
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/rayara-mutt-2/sri-raghavendra-swamigalu/
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raghavendra_Tirtha

nodes.name: Yogindra Tirtha
nodes.contrib: The chosen successor of Raghavendra Tirtha, who took charge of the mutt after his guru's vrindavana-pravesha. His own vrindavana is at Tiruchirapalli.
sources: https://madhwasakha.com/guru/shri-yogindra-teertharu/520
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/rayara-mutt-2/sri-raghavendra-swamigalu/

nodes.name: Suryindra (Sooreendra) Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Disciple of Yogindra Tirtha and himself the guru of Sumatindra Tirtha, whom Raghavendra had foretold as the third pontiff after him. His vrindavana is at Madurai.
sources: https://madhwasakha.com/guru/shri-suryindra-teertharu/521
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/rayara-mutt-2/soorendra-theertharu/

nodes.name: Sumatindra Tirtha
nodes.contrib: The third pontiff after Raghavendra Tirtha, whom his guru had singled out with the words that the third yati after him would carry his works forward; he is accordingly called the Vidyasuta (intellectual heir) of Raghavendra. A prolific author of more than forty works — commentaries, tippanis on the Sudha and Chandrika, and independent treatises — his vrindavana is at Srirangam.
sources: https://madhwasakha.com/guru/shri-sumatindra-teertharu/522
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sumatindra_Tirtha
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/rayara-mutt-2/sumateendraru/

nodes.name: Upendra Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Disciple of Sumatindra Tirtha and guru of Vadindra Tirtha, holding the seat briefly. His vrindavana is at Srirangam.
sources: https://madhwasakha.com/guru/shri-upendra-teertharu/523
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/rayara-mutt-2/upendra-tirtharu/

nodes.name: Vadindra (Vadeendra) Tirtha
nodes.purva: (great-grandson of Raghavendra in his purvashrama line)
nodes.contrib: The fifth pontiff after Raghavendra and, in his purvashrama descent, his great-grandson. Raghavendra is said to have reserved a vrindavana beside his own at Mantralaya for him in advance. He composed the Guruguna Stavana, thirty-six verses in praise of Raghavendra, and wrote tippanis on the Tatvaprakashika and Tatvodyota. His vrindavana stands to the left of Raghavendra's at Mantralaya.
sources: https://madhwasakha.com/guru/shri-vadeendra-teertharu/524
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/rayara-mutt-2/sri-vadeendra-theertharu/

nodes.name: Vasudhendra Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Disciple of Vadindra Tirtha and eldest of three brothers — sons of Raghavendra's purvashrama nephew Venugopalacharya — who each in turn led the mutt. He spent most of his tenure at Mantralaya and wrote a commentary on the Gurugunastavana. His vrindavana is at Kenchanagudda on the Tungabhadra near Siruguppa.
sources: https://madhwasakha.com/guru/shri-vasudhendra-teertharu/525
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/rayara-mutt-2/vasudendra-thirtha/

nodes.name: Varadendra Tirtha
nodes.contrib: The seventh pontiff after Raghavendra, of whom Raghavendra is said to have prophesied that the seventh would be his equal. A noted victor in debate — including against the Advaita pandit Ramashastri at Pune — under whom the mutt flourished and received land grants. He gave strong encouragement to Haridasa literature, teaching Jagannatha Dasa and Pranesha Dasa; the Varadendra Haridasa Sahitya Mandala at Lingasugur continues in his name. His moola vrindavana is at Pune and his mrittika vrindavana, the 'Swapna Vrindavana', at Lingasugur.
sources: https://madhwasakha.com/guru/shri-varadendra-teertharu/526
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/rayara-mutt-2/varadendra-theertharu/

nodes.name: Dheerendra Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Purvashrama son of Vadindra Tirtha, long reluctant to take sannyasa and much given to touring and preaching. He eventually received sannyasa directly before Vijayindra Tirtha's shrine at Kumbakonam, held the Mantralaya seat only briefly, and then settled at Hosaritti on the Varada river. He was close to Satyabodha Tirtha and Jagannatha Dasa, who is said to have composed the Harikathamrutasara in his presence. He wrote several commentaries on Upanishadic hymns.
sources: https://madhwasakha.com/guru/shri-dheerendra-teertharu/527
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/rayara-mutt-2/dheerendra-theertharu/

nodes.name: Bhuvanendra Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Youngest of the three brothers who successively led the mutt (after Vasudhendra and Varadendra). Ashrama disciple of Varadendra and student of Dheerendra Tirtha, to whom he offered the seat before taking charge himself. His vrindavana is at Rajoli.
sources: https://madhwasakha.com/guru/shri-bhuvanendra-teertharu/528
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/rayara-mutt-2/bhuvanendra-theertharu/

nodes.name: Subodhendra Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Disciple of Bhuvanendra Tirtha and guru of Sujanendra Tirtha. He received grants and support from Mummadi Krishnaraja Wodeyar of Mysore, including a choultry at Nanjangud, where his vrindavana stands.
sources: https://madhwasakha.com/guru/shri-subodhendra-teertharu/529
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/rayara-mutt-2/subodendra-tirtharu/

nodes.name: Sujanendra Tirtha
nodes.contrib: A renowned orator and debater who studied under Subodhendra Tirtha. In the Mysore court he defeated the celebrated Pune scholar Trayambaka Shastri, styled 'Abhinava Bhoja', in a debate on grammar, logic, mimamsa and Vedanta, earning grants for the mutt from Mummadi Krishnaraja Wodeyar. His vrindavana is at Nanjangud, installed together with his guru Subodhendra's.
sources: https://madhwasakha.com/guru/shri-sujanendra-teertharu/530
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/rayara-mutt-2/sujanendra-tirtharu/

nodes.name: Sujnanendra Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Great-grandson of Vadindra Tirtha and a noted tapasvi, credited in tradition with completing the Nyaya Sudha mangala eight times. He installed the celebrated stone image of Raghavendra found by a washerman at Srirangapatna, later consecrated at Nanjangud. His vrindavana is at Mantralaya.
sources: https://madhwasakha.com/guru/shri-sujnanendra-teertharu/531
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/rayara-mutt-2/sujnanendraru/

nodes.name: Sudharmendra Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Disciple of Sujnanendra Tirtha and guru of Sugunendra Tirtha, remembered in tradition for curing a disciple's affliction. His vrindavana is at Mantralaya.
sources: https://madhwasakha.com/guru/shri-sudharmendra-teertharu/532
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/rayara-mutt-2/sudharmendra-tirtharu/

nodes.name: Sugunendra Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Disciple of Sudharmendra Tirtha and guru of Suprajnendra Tirtha. His vrindavana is at Greamspet, Chittoor.
sources: https://madhwasakha.com/guru/shri-sugunendra-teertharu/533
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/rayara-mutt-2/sugunendra-tirtharu/

nodes.name: Suprajnendra Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Disciple of Sugunendra Tirtha, learned in kavya, nataka, alankara and Vedanta, and himself the vidya-guru of Susheelendra Tirtha. His vrindavana is at Nanjangud.
sources: https://madhwasakha.com/guru/shri-suprajnendra-teertharu/534
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/rayara-mutt-2/suprajnendra-tirtharu/

nodes.name: Sukrutheendra Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Disciple of Suprajnendra Tirtha and guru of Susheelendra Tirtha. His vrindavana is at Nanjangud.
sources: https://madhwasakha.com/guru/shri-sukrutheendra-teertharu/535
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/rayara-mutt-2/sukruteendra-tirtharu/

nodes.name: Susheelendra Tirtha
nodes.contrib: A pontiff active in institution-building who founded the Srimat-Sameera-Samaya-Samvardhini Sabha for dharma-prachara and the honouring of scholars, and sponsored Goudagere Venkataramanacharya's Chandrika Prakasha Prasara in reply to an Advaita critique of Vyasaraja's Chandrika. He consecrated a mrittika vrindavana of Raghavendra at Udupi at the Ashta Mathas' request. His own vrindavana is at Hosaritti near Savanur.
sources: https://madhwasakha.com/guru/shri-susheelendra-teertharu/536
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/rayara-mutt-2/susheelendra-tirtharu/

nodes.name: Suvratindra Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Disciple of Susheelendra Tirtha and guru of Suyamindra Tirtha, under whom the next generation of the mutt's scholars trained. His vrindavana is at Mantralaya.
sources: https://madhwasakha.com/guru/shri-suvratindra-teertharu/537
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/rayara-mutt-2/suvrateendra-tirtharu/

nodes.name: Suyamindra Tirtha
nodes.contrib: The thirty-sixth pontiff of the Rayara Mutt, trained in sahitya, veda, nyaya and Vedanta. He founded the mutt's magazine Parimala, began the Anna-Santarpane (free-feeding) scheme, built lodging for pilgrims, and established the mutt's branch at Subbarayanakere, Mysore. His vrindavana is at Mantralaya.
sources: https://madhwasakha.com/guru/shri-suyamindra-teertharu/538
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/rayara-mutt-2/suyameendra-tirtharu/

nodes.name: Sujayindra Tirtha
nodes.contrib: A builder-pontiff who founded the Gurusarvabhouma Vidyapitha, offering free board to students of Madhva shastra, and started the Gurusarvabhouma magazine, now issued in several languages. He renovated the Mantralaya establishment with schools, dining halls, hospitals and pilgrim facilities, earning the title Architect of Mantralaya. His vrindavana is at Mantralaya.
sources: https://madhwasakha.com/guru/shri-sujayindra-teertharu/539
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/rayara-mutt-2/sujayeendra-tirtharu/

nodes.name: Sushameendra Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Born at Nanjangud, he led the mutt from 1986 to 2009 and is affectionately remembered as the 'walking Rayaru' (Nadedaduva Rayaru) for his extensive touring among devotees. He initiated the development of the Shakambari Nagara Rayara Mutt. His vrindavana is at Mantralaya.
sources: https://madhwasakha.com/guru/shri-sushameendra-teertharu/540
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/rayara-mutt-2/sushmeendra-tirtharu/

nodes.name: Suyatindra Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Disciple of Sushameendra Tirtha, remembered as the rebuilder of modern Mantralaya after severe flooding, restoring the establishment with improved facilities. He named Subudhendra Tirtha his successor and attained his vrindavana at Mantralaya in 2014, on the aradhana day of Vyasaraja.
sources: https://madhwasakha.com/guru/shri-suyatindra-teertharu/541
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/rayara-mutt-2/suyateendra-tirtharu/

nodes.name: Subudhendra Tirtha
nodes.contrib: The present pontiff of the Rayara Mutt, born near Kurnool, chosen as successor by Suyatindra Tirtha and now the incumbent at Mantralaya.
sources: https://madhwasakha.com/guru/shri-subudhendra-teertharu/542
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/rayara-mutt-2/
nodes.role: present incumbent (Raghavendra Matha, Mantralaya)

nodes.name: Rajendra Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Passed over for the Uttaradi seat when away on tour; founder-ancestor of the Vyasaraja (Poorvadi) Matha line at Sosale.
sources: https://madhwayati.blogspot.com/2019/04/rajendra-teertharu-yeragola-1440-matha.html
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vidyadhiraja_Tirtha

nodes.name: Jayadhwaja Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Brother and successor of Rajendra Tirtha; guru of Purushottama Tirtha.
sources: https://madhwayati.blogspot.com/2019/05/vyasaraja-mutt-vyasa-teertha-matha.html

nodes.name: Purushottama Tirtha
nodes.brindavana: Abbur area (tradition: entered a cave alive, no ordinary brindavana)
nodes.contrib: Successor of Jayadhwaja; ordination-guru of Brahmanya Tirtha.
sources: https://madhwayati.blogspot.com/2019/04/purushottama-teertharu-1412-or-1478.html

nodes.name: Brahmanya Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Ordination guru of Vyasatirtha, whom he raised and named his successor.
sources: https://madhwayati.blogspot.com/2019/04/1467-brahmanya-teertharu-1467-abbur.html
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vyasatirtha

nodes.name: Vyasatirtha (Vyasaraja)
nodes.place: island in the Tungabhadra near Anegundi / Hampi
nodes.contrib: Peak dialectician of the school; kula-guru of Vijayanagara (esp. Krishnadevaraya). Organised the Dasakuta, institutionalising the Haridasa movement; traditionally consecrated 732 Mukhyaprana icons. Studied under Sripadaraja and Brahmanya Tirtha.
sources: Wikipedia: Vyasatirtha

nodes.name: Purandara Dasa
nodes.contrib: 'Pitamaha (father) of Carnatic music'; foremost of the Dasakuta.
sources: Wikipedia
Wikipedia: Purandara Dasa
nodes.note: Birthplace determined as Tirthahalli (Shivamogga) by a 2018 Govt. of Karnataka committee; earlier sources say Purandaragada.

nodes.name: Kanaka Dasa
nodes.contrib: Poet-saint of the Dasakuta; social reformer; celebrated bhakti composer.
sources: Wikipedia
Wikipedia: Kanaka Dasa

nodes.name: Srinivasa Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Pontifical successor of Vyasatirtha in the Sosale line.
sources: https://madhwayati.blogspot.com/2019/04/sreenivasa-teertharu-nava-vrundavana.html

nodes.name: Rama Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Line splits after him into Vyasaraja Matha (Sosale) and Vyasaraja Matha (Kundapura).
sources: https://madhwayati.blogspot.com/2019/05/vyasaraja-mutt-vyasa-teertha-matha.html

nodes.name: Lakshmikantha Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Disciple of Rama Tirtha and guru of Sripathi Tirtha, holding the Vyasaraja Matha seat 1584-1594. His vrindavana is at Penukonda.
sources: vyasarajamatha.org
Wikipedia
https://www.sumadhwaseva.com/yatigalu/vyasaraja-mutt/lakshmikantha-thirtharu/

nodes.name: Sripathi Tirtha
nodes.contrib: A pontiff praised as learned in every school (sarva-tantra-kovida), disciple of Lakshmikantha Tirtha and guru of Kambaluru Ramachandra Tirtha; he led the seat 1594-1612. His vrindavana is at Rayavellore.
sources: vyasarajamatha.org
Wikipedia

dhyana.deva:
विद्वत्पङ्कजमार्ताण्डो वादिमत्तेभकेसरी।
जगन्नाथगुरुर्भूयात् ज्यायसे श्रेयसे मम॥
dhyana.note: Dhyāna-śloka — “May Guru Jagannātha, the sun that unfolds the lotus-scholars, the lion among rutting debater-elephants, be for my greater good.”

bio.summary: Śrī Jagannātha Tīrtha — celebrated as Bhāṣyadīpikācārya after his masterwork — was the pontiff of the Vyāsarāja Maṭha from 1755 to 1770, with his bṛndāvana at Kumbhakoṇam. Tradition holds him to be an avatāra of Gālava Ṛṣi. He was among the very few Vyāsarāja Maṭha yatis to take saṁnyāsa directly from brahmacarya after Śrī Vyāsarāja himself. He studied for nearly thirty years under his guru Śrī Śeṣacandrikācārya, and his own commentaries on the Brahma-sūtra Bhāṣya remain indispensable to Mādhva students of every maṭha.
bio.origin: Born in Varavani village on the north bank of the Pinākinī (Pennār) river, Gauribidanūr tāluk, Kolār district. Kauṇḍinya gotra, Tangedi family (Ṣaṣṭika vaṁśa). His forebears held rights over five villages known together as the “Varavani Pañcagrāma”; the family deity was Narasiṁha at Honnappanahaḷḷi.

anecdotes.title: Saved by Narasiṁha from the mango tree
anecdotes.text: While travelling in the Tekkalu region of Tamil country he was pursued by hostile soldiers. He prayed to his family deity Narasiṁha, who burst forth from a nearby mango tree and destroyed the attackers. He recorded the deliverance in his own verse within the Bhāṣyadīpikā.

anecdotes.title: Swimming the Kāverī with the devara-peṭṭige
anecdotes.text: When soldiers tried to seize the devara-peṭṭige (the casket of the worship-icons and ornaments), he swam some twenty kilometres down the rushing Kāverī holding the sacred chest so that no unqualified hand should touch it. A sword-wound taken in the act would have disqualified him from ritual service, but his guru healed him within forty-eight days through special Narasiṁha worship.

anecdotes.title: How the title Bhāṣyadīpikācārya was won
anecdotes.text: One night his guru Śeṣacandrikācārya found the young ascetic asleep clutching a manuscript — the Bhāṣyadīpikā. On reading it he was astonished at its brilliance, conferred the honorific “Bhāṣyadīpikācārya,” and reinstated him as successor. The place where he composed his works — the Bhāvan Kalmaṇṭapam — still bears his image carved on a pillar.

verses.deva:
आम्रस्तम्भात् समागत्य ताम्रतुण्डान् निहत्य यः।
नम्रं नौमि जगन्नाथं ताम्रोपात्तं नृकेसरी॥
verses.iast: āmrastambhāt samāgatya tāmratuṇḍān nihatya yaḥ | namraṃ naumi jagannāthaṃ tāmropāttaṃ nṛkesarī ||
verses.note: His own verse on the man-lion (Nṛkesarī) who came forth from the mango-pillar and struck down the copper-armed foe — from the Bhāṣyadīpikā. (Reading normalised from the two source sites.)

nodes.name: Bhandarkere (Bhandarakeri) Matha
nodes.period: Tulu-region Madhva matha; antiquity claim traditional
nodes.contrib: Deity Kodandarama; tradition traces it to Achyutapreksha -> Satya Tirtha. Vishnu-Tirtha link NOT attested; real pairing is with Bhimanakatte. ~32 heads to present Vidyesha Tirtha.
sources: https://madhwayati.blogspot.com/2019/06/a-19-bhandarakeri-matha-mutt.html
nodes.note: Antiquity beyond ~15th c. undocumented; the Achyutapreksha descent is prestige tradition.

nodes.name: Bhimanakatte Matha
nodes.contrib: Original name 'Achyutapreksha Tirtha Samsthana'; ~41 heads (present Raghuvarendra Tirtha). Follows the Achyutapreksha/Madhva line.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhimanakatte_matha
https://madhwasakha.com/math-details/shri-bhimanakatte-math/20
nodes.note: The ~5,035-year / Durvasa-Janamejaya antiquity claim is legend, not history.

nodes.name: Balagaru Akshobhya Tirtha Matha
nodes.period: founded by Akshobhya Tirtha's initiation of Lokavandita Tirtha
nodes.contrib: Akshobhya-family matha; ~12 brindavanas (many unidentified); records lost in floods, so chronology is undocumented rather than legendary.
sources: https://madhwasakha.com/math-details/shri-balagaru-math/18

nodes.name: Kudli Arya Akshobhya Tirtha Matha
nodes.contrib: ~32 heads (present Raghu Vijaya Tirtha). Claims Akshobhya's seat.
sources: https://www.kudlimath.in/
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akshobhya_Tirtha
nodes.note: Brindavana ambiguity: standard references place Akshobhya at Malkhed; the Kudli math centres him at Kudli - competing traditions.

nodes.name: Kukke Subrahmanya Matha
nodes.contrib: Founded by Vishnu Tirtha (Madhva's brother); succeeded at Subrahmanya by Aniruddha Tirtha. Best-attested 'Madhva's brother' foundation. Present head Vidyaprasanna Tirtha.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subramanya_Matha
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vishnu_Tirtha

nodes.name: Vijaya Dasa
nodes.contrib: Revived the Dasakuta in the 18th c.; ~25,000 suladis, ugabhogas and padas; initiated (in a dream at Gaya) into Purandara Dasa's stream; guru of Gopala Dasa, Mohana Dasa and Venugopala Dasa.
sources: Wikipedia
Wikipedia: Vijaya Dasa
madhwayati.blogspot.com

nodes.name: Gopala Dasa
nodes.contrib: Prolific Dasakuta composer; disciple of Vijaya Dasa and guru of Jagannatha Dasa; also renowned as an astrologer; inspired Helavanakatte Giriyamma.
sources: Wikipedia
Wikipedia: Gopala Dasa
madhwayati.blogspot.com

nodes.name: Jagannatha Dasa
nodes.contrib: Author of the Harikathamruthasara (Bhamini Shatpadi, 32 sandhis / 988 stanzas), a summa of Dvaita in Kannada; disciple of Gopala Dasa; also studied under Varadendra Tirtha.
sources: Wikipedia
Wikipedia: Jagannatha Dasa (Kannada poet)

nodes.name: Mohana Dasa
nodes.contrib: Foster son and disciple of Vijaya Dasa; one of his three foremost disciples of the 18th-c. Dasakuta revival.
sources: Wikipedia: Vijaya Dasa
Wikipedia: Haridasa
nodes.note: Foster son of Vijaya Dasa; precise dates not firmly documented.

nodes.name: Venugopala Dasa (Panganama Timmanna)
nodes.contrib: A Diwan (minister) who became a disciple of Vijaya Dasa; counted among his three foremost disciples.
sources: Wikipedia: Vijaya Dasa
Wikipedia: Haridasa

nodes.name: Helavanakatte Giriyamma
nodes.contrib: One of the earliest women poet-saints of the Haridasa tradition; inspired to compose devotional songs by Gopala Dasa.
sources: Wikipedia: Gopala Dasa
Wikipedia: Haridasa
nodes.note: Woman saint of the Dasakuta; precise dates not firmly documented.

nodes.name: Prasanna Venkata Dasa
nodes.contrib: 18th-c. Dasakuta poet-saint of Bagalkot; tradition holds his ankita was bestowed by Lord Venkateshwara at Tirumala.
sources: Wikipedia: Prasanna Venkata Dasa
Wikipedia: Haridasa
nodes.note: Placed on the Purandara/Dasakuta stream for grouping; a firmly-documented dasa-diksha guru is not attested in accessible sources.

nodes.name: Kakhandaki Mahipati Dasa
nodes.contrib: 17th-c. saint, scholar and minister of the Haridasa tradition at Kakhandaki; revered even by the Adil Shahi rulers of Bijapur.
sources: Wikipedia: Mahipati Dasa
Wikipedia: Haridasa
nodes.note: Independent 17th-c. Haridasa (Kakhandaki stream); shown on the Dasa branch for grouping — no documented dasa-diksha to Purandara.
